name: Shiphrah
overview: Shiphrah is a female Hebrew midwife mentioned in the book of Exodus. She is recognized for her role during the time when the Israelites were in Egypt. Scripture identifies her specifically as a midwife, highlighting her unique contribution to the preservation of Hebrew lives.
namesAndTitles: The name Shiphrah means "beautiful" or "fair." This proper name, as recorded in Exodus 1:15, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that may reflect her character or role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Shiphrah beyond her identification as a Hebrew midwife. No additional relationships are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shiphrah's significance lies in her role as a Hebrew midwife during a critical period for the Israelites in Egypt. Her work would have been vital in the survival of Hebrew children under difficult circumstances. Though details are limited, her mention underscores God's providential care through ordinary individuals fulfilling His purposes.
